title: Implement copy constructors for custom data objects
body: For example, for SynthesisRun, SynthesisGoal, etc. As it is, the lack of copy constructors makes it difficult to create deep clones of hashmaps and so on, which causes various issues with storing safely immutable data.

title: ULTIMATE hangs for a few seconds after synthesis
body: ULTIMATE will freeze for a bit after running synthesis. I think this is because EvoChecker is saving the Pareto set file more than once, or the file-reading function is inefficient.

title: Handle temporary files correctly
body: Temporary files aren't deleted correctly when ULTIMATE is done with them. The Pareto set file should also be a temporary file rather than being saved to the program directory.

title: Create UltimateException class
body: Create an UltimateException class for better error handling. There are many issues that can occur when ULTIMATE models are incorrectly formatted or constructed which are not captured well by Java's basic exception types. For example, out-of-bounds dependencyParameters should be detected and an UltimateException should be thrown.

title: Edge cases when component models are altered between loads.
body:
ULTIMATE can get confused when component models are altered inbetween loads of the world model. For example, if a constant is renamed, and that constant corresponded to an external parameter in the world model, then the GUI will still display the external parameter with the old name alongside a new uncategorised parameter with the new name. Removing the old external parameter will create an uncategorised parameter with that old name, which is impossible to remove.

One possible solution would be to check that each parameter still exists when the world model is loaded. If it does not, flag it with a message to the effect of "this parameter name could not be found in this model". If a parameter with this tag is removed from a model, it is not added to the uncategorised parameters. (Alternatively, but more advanced: allow the user to specify the new name of the parameter so that it does not need to be delted).

title: ULTIMATE closes if certain errors are encountered.
body: ULTIMATE will sometimes exit whenever a recoverable error is encountered (e.g. if there is a syntax error in a model during synthesis). This is probably because of an overzealous use of System.exit(1), which was appropriate for the headless version but not the GUI.

title: Switch to ULTIMATE API, Adding Synthesis to GUI
body:
Additions:

- Synthesis GUI:
    - Add and remove synthesis objectives in the properties tab
    - Click 'synthesise' (next to verify) to run synthesis
    - Synthesis results are shown underneath verification results
    - Checking 'Plot Pareto Front' will use EvoChecker to do so after the results are obtained
    - Pareto fronts and sets are automatically saved (via EvoChecker). Check the console output to see the directory.
- Internal parameters:
    - Internal parameters are now properly implemented (pending discovery of any bugs, of course)
    - Can be added just like any other parameter type via the GUI
    - Properly saved and loaded to .ultimate files.
    - Cannot perform verification on models with internal parameters (alert will be shown)
- Usability:
    - Progress is now shown for ranged verification
    - The text of all results is now selectable, so that they can be copy-pasted.
- Case studies:
    - Added a case study called 'RangedVerificationExample', which is a duplicate of the robofleet case study with some ranged parameters.
    
(Temporary) Removals:

- Cannot plot ranged verification results
- Cannot export results
- These will be restored momentarily!

Invisible Changes:

- Verification and synthesis now goes through the Ultimate class (the ULTIMATE API). Previously, logic for verification was implemented in the UI classes and then again seperately in the headless class, which meant that there was a lot of code reuse, and the main verification code was mixed with UI code. Now, the verification code is all in one place, which should help to extend/bug fix it in the future. Some more work is needed to properly factor out the functionalitiy of the UI and API.
- Restructured parameters. Previously, parameters did not inherit from one another or share any interfaces, which made them difficult to extend. They have now been restructured around the IParameter interface. The various ExternalParameter have been seperated into different classes for fixed, ranged, and learned, all extending a common ExternalParameter abstract class. Hopefully this will make future development smoother.
- Restructured caching. The previous caching behaviour used various, mutually-incompatible formats for the cache keys. Now, all caching goes through the Project class, so adjusting the behaviour will be a lot easier. This will be necessary if we want to extend caching to dependency parameters. I believe that this restructuring also fixed a few bugs.
- Restructured ranged experiments. Previously the ranged experiment code was quite opaque, and the verification worked in a slightly different way to the verification of non-ranged models. This has been restructured (and properly commented) so it should now be more intuitive. The results of the verification, which were previously stored in strings in a UI element, are now properly stored in an array of new RangedVerificationResults objects. This will make it much easier to plot and export them later.

title: Inconsistent syntax for property verification
body:
For some of the current case studies, the syntax used to specify properties is inconsistent, particularly in the use of escape characters. For example, DPM-FX has:

R{\\"time\\"}=?[F \\"done\\"]
R{"power"}=?[C<=10000]

within the same ULTIMATE model (albeit on the FX and DPM models respectively).

The inconsistency is especially an issue with the headless version. If I run:

`java -cp target/ultimate_model_manager-1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar main.Headless -pf ../case_studies/DPM-FX\ Dynamic\ power\ mgmt\ for\ foreign\ exchange/FX.ultimate -m FX -p [property]`

then I'll get very different results depending on what I supply for [property]:

R{\\"time\\"}=?[F \\"done\\"] : syntax error
R{"time"}=?[F"done"] : undeclared identifier "time"
'R{"time"}=?[F"done"]' : reward structure contains non-finite rewards
'R{\\"time\\"}=?[F \\"done\\"]' : this works
(nothing, removing -p) : this works (verifies the same property)

There's also differences between reward and probability properties, e.g.:

`java -cp target/ultimate_model_manager-1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar main.Headless -pf ../case_studies/RoboFleet\ Mobile\ robot\ fleet/robotnav.ultimate -m robot1 -p Pmax=?[F"done"]`

gives the correct result even though this syntax does not work for a reward property.

Possible solutions:
- Stick to a basic syntax without escape characters and smartly convert to whatever format the current model checker (STORM/PRISM)

title: Altering individual model files requires ULTIMATE restart to reflect changes
body:
During the verification of properties by ULTIMATE, a number of temporary model instances are created and stored in /tmp. If the model from which one such instance was derived was altered on the disc and ULTIMATE is re-run, the program seems to use the original instance file without generating a new one (despite the changes being reflected in the "Model File" tab). The whole ULTIMATE project has to be re-loaded for the model changes to be reflected.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open a case study (say SMD)
2. Verify some property (say the one property in "SmartLighting"). A file called something like SmartLighting_copy576336546799547524.prism will be generated in /tmp
3. Navigate to SmartLighting.prism on the disc and introduce a syntax error.
4. Re-run the property verification. The result will be identical and the error will not be noticed. The logs will state that the original temp file (SmartLighting_copy576336546799547524.prism) is still being passed to STORM.

Possible solutions:
- A "reload models from disc" button that deletes any internal reference to the temp files
- Automatically check if the model files have changed when a property is verified or a parameter is added/altered
